items.caption:
Daniela Amodei says chatbots with ads end up telling you you're right.

Her point: competitors are putting ads into their chatbots, and ads pay more the longer a user stays engaged. So you don't want to tell that user they're wrong, which is why she thinks many of these products will almost inevitably end up with a sycophancy problem.

Would you trust an AI assistant that runs ads?

Source: The Builders with Walter Isaacson, Dario & Daniela Amodei. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=1OdoSzfUkec

items.caption:
Dario Amodei says Anthropic has caught its AI thinking one thing and telling the user another.

He explains mechanistic interpretability as giving the model an x-ray or brain scan to look inside at its motivations. Looking inside, they have caught the model thinking "X is actually true, but I'm going to tell the user Y."

Should every AI company be required to look inside its models like this?

items.caption:
Sam Altman says OpenAI went from okay at grade-school math to a Millennium Prize problem in three summers.

Three summers ago they were only okay at grade-school math. Two summers ago, a good to very good score on the AIME high school competition. One summer ago, an IMO gold medal, barely. And this summer, he says, they solved the Millennium Prize problem.

What do you think AI solves in the next three summers?

Source: Fortune, Titans and Disruptors: Sam Altman. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=2my-NU6LuCM
